name: Enforce image policy with VAP
objective: CKS › Supply Chain Security (20%). Drill EVERY supply-chain corner harder than the exam: Trivy CVE scanning with severity gates, static manifest analysis with kubesec, digest pinning, banning :latest, ImagePullPolicy hardening, an approved-registry ValidatingAdmissionPolicy + binding, a VAP that bans :latest, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix on a broken binding. questions.title: Approved-registry admission (ValidatingAdmissionPolicy)
questions.teach:
A **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (VAP)** enforces rules in-cluster with **CEL** — no webhook server. An approved-registry allowlist uses `object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.k8s.io/'))`, matched on Pods via `matchConstraints`.

**Gotcha:** the policy does **nothing** until a **binding** references it by `policyName` with `validationActions: [Deny]`.
questions.prompt:
Create a **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy** `approved-registry` that denies Pods whose container images do NOT start with `registry.k8s.io/`, plus a **ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding** `approved-registry-binding` enabling it (action `Deny`) on Pods.

Target: both objects exist; the policy's CEL validation references `registry.k8s.io` over `object.spec.containers`; the binding has `policyName: approved-registry` and `validationActions` containing `Deny`.
questions.hint: `matchConstraints.resourceRules` on resource `pods` (apiGroups `[""]`). Validation CEL: `object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.k8s.io/'))`. Binding: `policyName: approved-registry`, `validationActions: [Deny]`, `matchResources: {}`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: approved-registry
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations: ["CREATE","UPDATE"]
      resources: ["pods"]
  validations:
  - expression: "object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.k8s.io/'))"
    message: "images must come from registry.k8s.io"
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: approved-registry-binding
spec:
  policyName: approved-registry
  validationActions: ["Deny"]
  matchResources: {}
YAML

verification.description: VAP approved-registry + binding with the registry.k8s.io rule and Deny

questions.eli5:
Picture a nightclub with a bouncer at the door. Every pod that wants into the cluster has to walk past this bouncer first. A **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (VAP)** is a rulebook you hand the built-in bouncer — the API server itself. No extra staff, no separate security company; the bouncer is already there and just needs rules.

Your rule here: *"only let in pods whose container images come from `registry.k8s.io/`."* You write it in a mini-language called **CEL**:

```
object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.k8s.io/'))
```

Read it as: "for **all** containers `c`, the image must start with `registry.k8s.io/`." If any container fails, the bouncer turns the pod away.

But here's the twist that trips everyone up: writing the rulebook (`ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`) does **nothing** by itself. You also have to officially *hand it to the bouncer and say "enforce this"* — that's the **Binding** (`ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding`), with `validationActions: [Deny]`.

**But watch out:**

- **A policy with no binding enforces nothing.** It just sits on a shelf. You need BOTH objects.
- The binding needs **`validationActions: [Deny]`** to actually block. `Warn` or `Audit` only log — bad pods still get in.
- The binding's **`policyName` must exactly match** the policy's `metadata.name`, or it points at nothing.
- `matchConstraints` on the policy says *which objects* the rule even looks at (here, Pods). Get the resource/apiGroup wrong and it silently never fires.
- `.all()` over an **empty** container list returns **true** — an edge case, though real pods always have containers.
questions.deepDive:
## Approved-registry enforcement with ValidatingAdmissionPolicy — full rundown

### Mental model
A **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (VAP)** runs admission checks **inside the API server** using **CEL** (Common Expression Language) — no external webhook server to deploy, TLS to manage, or pod to keep alive. It replaces much of what you'd previously build with ImagePolicyWebhook / OPA-Gatekeeper / Kyverno for simple validation. VAP has **two objects**:

1. **`ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`** — *what* to check (the CEL rules + which resources they apply to).
2. **`ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding`** — *activate* the policy and say *how* to react (`Deny`/`Warn`/`Audit`) and *where*.

A policy without a binding is **inert**.

### The policy
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: approved-registry
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail                 # if CEL errors, reject (vs Ignore)
  matchConstraints:                   # which admission requests this looks at
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   [""]               # core group for pods
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE","UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["pods"]
  validations:
  - expression: "object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.k8s.io/'))"
    message: "images must come from registry.k8s.io"
```

### The binding (activates it)
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: approved-registry-binding
spec:
  policyName: approved-registry       # MUST match the policy's metadata.name
  validationActions: ["Deny"]         # Deny | Warn | Audit (list)
  matchResources: {}                  # {} = all requests the policy's matchConstraints select
```

### Key spec fields
| Field | Object | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `matchConstraints.resourceRules` | policy | which GVR + operations are evaluated |
| `validations[].expression` | policy | CEL that must return **true** to admit |
| `validations[].message` | policy | denial message |
| `failurePolicy` | policy | `Fail` (reject on CEL error) or `Ignore` |
| `policyName` | binding | links binding → policy by name |
| `validationActions` | binding | `Deny` / `Warn` / `Audit` |
| `matchResources` | binding | optionally narrow the policy's scope (e.g. by namespace labels) |

### CEL essentials for images
| Expression | Checks |
|---|---|
| `object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image.startsWith('registry.k8s.io/'))` | every container from approved registry |
| `object.spec.containers.exists(c, c.image.contains(':latest'))` | any container uses :latest |
| `object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))` | no container uses :latest |
| `size(object.spec.containers)` | container count |

`object` is the incoming resource. `.all(var, expr)` is true when `expr` holds for every element (and **true for an empty list**); `.exists(...)` is true if any element matches.

### validationActions
| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `Deny` | request **rejected** |
| `Warn` | admitted; warning returned to the client |
| `Audit` | admitted; recorded in the audit log annotation |

Only `Deny` enforces. You can combine (e.g. `["Deny"]`, or `["Warn","Audit"]` to observe before enforcing).

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Policy alone enforces nothing** — you must create the **binding** too.
- **`validationActions` must include `Deny`** to block. `Warn`/`Audit` only log; bad pods are admitted.
- **`binding.policyName` must exactly equal `policy.metadata.name`.** A typo'd/non-existent name is accepted silently and enforces nothing.
- **`matchConstraints` must actually select pods** — core group is `apiGroups: [""]`, `resources: ["pods"]`. Wrong GVR → never fires.
- **VAP checks only the object under admission** — it does not evaluate initContainers/ephemeralContainers unless your CEL includes them (`object.spec.initContainers`). For full coverage, check all three lists.
- **`.all()` over an empty list is `true`** — usually harmless for pods but important for CEL reasoning.
- `failurePolicy: Fail` means a *buggy* CEL expression rejects everything it matches — test carefully.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl apply -f approved-registry.yaml      # policy + binding (---)
kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicy approved-registry
kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicybinding approved-registry-binding

# should be DENIED (wrong registry):
kubectl run bad --image=nginx:1.25 --dry-run=server
# should be ADMITTED:
kubectl run ok --image=registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9 --dry-run=server
```

questions.title: Ban :latest cluster-wide with a VAP
questions.teach:
The same VAP mechanism can **ban `:latest`**: a CEL check `object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))` rejects any Pod whose container image ends in `:latest`. It pairs with its own binding, independent of the registry policy.

**Gotcha:** this does NOT catch an untagged image (`nginx`) — `endsWith(':latest')` is false for it; catching that needs a stricter CEL (`c.image.contains(':') || c.image.contains('@')`).
questions.prompt:
Create a **ValidatingAdmissionPolicy** `no-latest-tag` that denies Pods with a container image ending in `:latest`, plus a binding `no-latest-tag-binding` enabling it (action `Deny`) on Pods.

Target: both objects exist; the policy's CEL validation references `:latest` with `endsWith` over `object.spec.containers`; the binding has `policyName: no-latest-tag` and `validationActions` containing `Deny`.
questions.hint: Validation CEL: `object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))`. Then a binding with `policyName: no-latest-tag`, `validationActions: [Deny]`, `matchResources: {}`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: no-latest-tag
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations: ["CREATE","UPDATE"]
      resources: ["pods"]
  validations:
  - expression: "object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))"
    message: "the :latest tag is banned"
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: no-latest-tag-binding
spec:
  policyName: no-latest-tag
  validationActions: ["Deny"]
  matchResources: {}
YAML

verification.description: VAP no-latest-tag + binding banning :latest with Deny

questions.eli5:
Same bouncer, new rule. Earlier you told the API-server bouncer "only images from `registry.k8s.io/`." Now you give it a second, independent rule: *"turn away any pod whose image name ends in `:latest`."*

Why? `:latest` is a moving target — it points at whatever was pushed last, so nobody can be sure what code is really running. Banning it cluster-wide forces everyone to name a real version.

The CEL rule reads almost like English:

```
object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))
```

"For **all** containers `c`, the image must **not** end with `:latest`." The `!` means "not." If any container ends in `:latest`, the bouncer says no.

And just like before, the rulebook needs its own **Binding** with `validationActions: [Deny]` to actually enforce. This policy and binding are a separate pair from the registry one — they don't share anything.

**But watch out:**

- **`endsWith(':latest')` misses untagged images!** `nginx` (no tag) secretly means `nginx:latest`, but the string `nginx` does **not** end in `:latest`, so it sneaks through. To catch that too you'd need a stricter rule like *"the image must contain a `:` or an `@`"* (`c.image.contains(':') || c.image.contains('@')`).
- Still needs **both** objects — policy plus binding — and **`Deny`**, not `Warn`/`Audit`.
- The binding's **`policyName` must match** `no-latest-tag` exactly.
- It only inspects `spec.containers` as written — initContainers aren't covered unless you add them.
questions.deepDive:
## Banning `:latest` cluster-wide with a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy — full rundown

### Mental model
The same VAP machinery that enforces an approved registry can forbid the `:latest` tag. You author a second, **independent** `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` + `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` pair whose CEL rejects any pod with a container image ending in `:latest`. Each policy/binding pair is self-contained — this one shares nothing with the registry policy.

### The policy
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: no-latest-tag
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE","UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["pods"]
  validations:
  - expression: "object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))"
    message: "the :latest tag is banned"
```

### The binding
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: no-latest-tag-binding
spec:
  policyName: no-latest-tag          # must match the policy name
  validationActions: ["Deny"]
  matchResources: {}
```

### The CEL rule, decoded
```
object.spec.containers.all(c, !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))
```
- `object` — the pod being admitted.
- `.all(c, …)` — true only if the inner expression holds for **every** container.
- `!c.image.endsWith(':latest')` — each image must **not** end in `:latest`.
- Result `true` → admit; `false` → the binding's action (Deny) fires.

### What this catches vs misses
| Image | `endsWith(':latest')` | Blocked by this rule? |
|---|---|---|
| `nginx:latest` | true | ✅ denied |
| `repo/app:latest` | true | ✅ denied |
| `nginx:1.25` | false | ✔ admitted (correct) |
| **`nginx`** (untagged) | **false** | ❌ **admitted** — but it *is* `:latest`! |
| `nginx@sha256:…` | false | ✔ admitted (correct) |

### Closing the untagged gap
`endsWith(':latest')` does not see the **implicit** `:latest` of an untagged image, because the literal string has no tag. A stricter policy requires every image to carry an explicit tag or digest:
```yaml
validations:
- expression: >-
    object.spec.containers.all(c, (c.image.contains(':') || c.image.contains('@'))
      && !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))
  message: "images must be explicitly tagged or digest-pinned, and not :latest"
```
(Refinement: a registry with a port, e.g. `registry:5000/app`, also contains a `:` — real-world rules often combine a registry-prefix allowlist with a digest/tag requirement.)

### CEL string helpers
| Function | Use |
|---|---|
| `s.startsWith(p)` | registry allowlist |
| `s.endsWith(p)` | tag suffix check |
| `s.contains(p)` | presence of `:` / `@` |
| `s.matches(re)` | RE2 regex match |

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Untagged images slip through** `endsWith(':latest')` — they resolve to `:latest` at runtime but the string doesn't. Add a `contains(':')||contains('@')` requirement to close it.
- **Both objects are required**, and the binding must use **`Deny`** — `Warn`/`Audit` only log.
- **`policyName` must equal `no-latest-tag`** exactly; a mismatch enforces nothing silently.
- **Only `spec.containers` is checked** as written — `initContainers`/`ephemeralContainers` need their own clauses.
- This is an **independent** pair; it does not interact with the registry policy. Deploy each with its own binding.
- `failurePolicy: Fail` + a buggy expression will reject matching pods wholesale — validate before relying on it.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl apply -f no-latest.yaml       # policy + binding
# denied:
kubectl run x --image=nginx:latest --dry-run=server
# admitted:
kubectl run y --image=nginx:1.25-alpine --dry-run=server
# NOTE: untagged slips through this simple rule:
kubectl run z --image=nginx --dry-run=server
```

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a VAP binding that enforces nothing
questions.teach:
A **ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding** is inert unless its `policyName` names a real policy AND `validationActions` includes `Deny`. Inspect with `kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicybinding <b> -o yaml` and compare `policyName` to the actual policy name and the action.

**Gotcha:** a binding pointing at a non-existent policy is accepted silently — it just never enforces, so bad Pods sail through.
questions.prompt:
A policy `block-privileged` exists, but its binding `block-privileged-binding` (seeded by setup) **enforces nothing** — privileged Pods are still admitted. Diagnose why and fix the binding so it actually enforces `block-privileged` with action `Deny`. Don't delete and recreate from scratch — find and fix what's wrong.

Target: binding `block-privileged-binding` has `policyName: block-privileged` and `validationActions` containing `Deny`.
questions.hint: `kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding -o yaml` — the `policyName` points at a wrong/typo'd policy and/or `validationActions` isn't `Deny`. Patch it: `kubectl patch validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"policyName":"block-privileged","validationActions":["Deny"]}}'`.
questions.solution:
# The seeded binding references a wrong policyName and action Warn — it enforces nothing.
kubectl patch validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"policyName":"block-privileged","validationActions":["Deny"]}}'

verification.description: block-privileged-binding now targets block-privileged with Deny

questions.eli5:
You've got a bouncer (the API server), a perfectly good rulebook on the shelf called `block-privileged`, and a work order (the **Binding**) that's supposed to say "bouncer, enforce that rulebook — turn people away." But privileged pods keep strolling in. Something on the work order is wrong.

There are only two things that can be broken on a binding, so this is a quick detective job:

1. **It names the wrong rulebook.** The binding's `policyName` has a typo or points at a policy that doesn't exist. The bouncer dutifully looks for "block-privilegd" (or whatever), can't find it, and shrugs — so nothing is enforced. (Kubernetes accepts this silently; it never warns you the target is missing.)
2. **The action is too soft.** `validationActions` is set to `Warn` or `Audit` — which only writes a note — instead of `Deny`, which actually blocks.

You fix it in place (don't delete and rebuild): read the binding, spot the wrong `policyName` and/or action, and **patch** both to `policyName: block-privileged` and `validationActions: [Deny]`.

**But watch out:**

- **A binding pointing at a missing policy is accepted silently.** No error, no event — it just never enforces. That silence is the trap.
- **`Warn`/`Audit` look "configured" but enforce nothing.** Only `Deny` blocks.
- The task says **fix, don't recreate** — use `kubectl patch`, keep the object.
- Check **both** fields — the name *and* the action can both be wrong at once.
- A merge-patch on `validationActions` **replaces the whole list**, so include every action you want (`["Deny"]`).
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnose & fix: a VAP binding that enforces nothing — full rundown

### Mental model
A `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` is only active when a `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` correctly **links to it** (`policyName`) **and** reacts hard enough (`validationActions` includes `Deny`). When privileged pods are admitted despite a `block-privileged` policy existing, the fault is almost always in the **binding**: wrong `policyName`, or an action of `Warn`/`Audit` instead of `Deny`. Both failures are accepted silently — nothing errors, so you must inspect.

### Diagnose
```bash
kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding -o yaml
kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicy                     # list real policy names
```
Compare two things against reality:

| Check | Correct value | Common breakage |
|---|---|---|
| `spec.policyName` | `block-privileged` (an existing policy) | typo / stale name → points at nothing |
| `spec.validationActions` | contains `Deny` | `["Warn"]` or `["Audit"]` → logs only |

Confirm the policy actually exists and its CEL is sound:
```bash
kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicy block-privileged -o yaml
```

### Fix in place (do NOT delete & recreate)
```bash
kubectl patch validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"policyName":"block-privileged","validationActions":["Deny"]}}'
```
A `--type=merge` patch on these scalar/array fields overwrites them: `policyName` is set, and `validationActions` is **replaced** by `["Deny"]`.

Alternative edit paths:
```bash
kubectl edit validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding
# or JSON patch for a single field:
kubectl patch validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding --type=json \
  -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/validationActions","value":["Deny"]},
       {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/policyName","value":"block-privileged"}]'
```

### Verify it now enforces
```bash
kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.policyName}{" "}{.spec.validationActions}{"\n"}'
# block-privileged ["Deny"]

# a privileged pod should now be rejected:
kubectl run priv --image=nginx \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"priv","image":"nginx","securityContext":{"privileged":true}}]}}' \
  --dry-run=server
```

### Why the failures are silent
- A binding whose `policyName` names a **non-existent** policy is **accepted** by the API server — there is no referential-integrity check at write time. It simply evaluates nothing.
- `validationActions: ["Warn"]`/`["Audit"]` are *valid* configurations — they admit the request and only emit a warning / audit annotation. The object looks healthy; it just doesn't block.

### validationActions recap
| Action | Admitted? | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| `Deny` | ❌ rejected | error to client |
| `Warn` | ✅ | `Warning:` header |
| `Audit` | ✅ | audit-log annotation |

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Silent acceptance of a dangling `policyName`** is the core trap — always compare the binding's `policyName` to the real policy list.
- **`Warn`/`Audit` masquerade as enforcement.** Only `Deny` blocks; check the action, not just that a binding exists.
- **Both fields can be wrong simultaneously** — fix the name *and* the action.
- **"Fix, don't recreate"** — use `kubectl patch`/`edit`; deleting and re-applying may be disallowed by the grader and loses the object's identity.
- A **merge patch replaces the entire `validationActions` array** — list every action you intend to keep.
- If pods *still* get through after the fix, verify the **policy's own** `matchConstraints`/CEL and `failurePolicy` — the bug may partly live in the policy, not only the binding.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding -o yaml   # inspect
kubectl patch validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"policyName":"block-privileged","validationActions":["Deny"]}}'  # fix
kubectl get validatingadmissionpolicybinding block-privileged-binding \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.policyName}{" "}{.spec.validationActions}{"\n"}'           # verify
```
